description: Equipe do Orbit Crew para o desafio Be An Earth System Trend Detective!
summary: Trend Detective Globe is an interactive 3D globe that helps students and the public tell a real climate trend from natural year-to-year variation. The user picks an Earth-science variable (temperature, rainfall, humidity, solar radiation, clouds, wind or soil moisture), clicks any place on the planet (or the whole world), chooses the years, and the tool builds the time series from NASA POWER data. It then measures the rate of change and tests significance with Mann-Kendall and a linear-regression t-test (95% confidence), and explains in plain language whether the change is a trend. The globe also colors the chosen region by the result, and a fire mode shows what share of a region is burning right now using NASA FIRMS/MODIS detections.
details: What it does: the user chooses (1) a variable, (2) a region by clicking the globe (point, 300 km, 800 km, or world sample), (3) a period and month, and gets (4) the time series and (5) a significance test. We compute the linear rate of change per decade with a 95% confidence interval, the Sen slope, the Mann-Kendall test and the regression t-test (significant when p < 0.05), and compare the total change with the typical year-to-year variation to show whether it is a trend or natural variability. Results are explained in plain language, with a chart showing the series, trend line and confidence band. The chosen region is painted on the globe (red = rising, blue = falling, gray = no clear trend). A fire mode shows the share of a region with active fire in the last 48 hours; this is a snapshot, not a trend. Data: NASA POWER (monthly, 1981 to last full year) and NASA FIRMS/MODIS active fires. No simulated data is used. Tools: JavaScript, three.js (WebGL), Vite, Cloudflare Pages. The globe landscape (biomes, rivers, mountains) is an illustrative, hand-drawn visual layer and is not scientific data. Natural Earth land shapes via world-atlas. Super Intelligence: the code and the user interface text were written with the help of Claude (Anthropic), and the team reviewed and directed the work. No SI-generated images or audio are used.
